correctness.rationale: For every nontrivial FAT coloring of a cycle, degree two forces alpha to be 1/2 or 1. The normalization identity then leaves only three parameter cases: proper two-coloring, half-half two-coloring, and proper three-coloring. Their cyclic closure conditions are respectively 2|n, 4|n, and 3|n, with uniqueness counts 1, 2, and 1 as unlabeled partitions. A direct refinement comparison shows all nontrivial classified colorings are maximal, while the trivial coloring is maximal exactly when it is the only one. Exact enumeration through n=12 independently matches the classification and count.

originality.rationale: The closest source is not merely silent: Beers--Mulas Example 5.12 gives a different irreducible-count classification for cycles, claiming exactly one outside multiples of six. The explicit C4 half-half partitions falsify that statement. Shaebani later exhaustively treats C6 and rules out the half-half case there, which is consistent with the new iff condition 4|n. Targeted database and web searches found no source giving the corrected divisibility-by-four family or the formula I(C_n)=1+2 1_{4|n}+1_{6|n}.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification on the canonical cycle family for a newly introduced coloring invariant. It identifies an infinite family of omitted irreducible colorings, gives the exact divisibility boundary and count, and corrects an explicit published-preprint family statement rather than adding a routine numerical example. The result also reconciles the later C6 exhaustive analysis with the corrected general picture.
